question: Simple interest on a certain sum is one-fifth of the sum and the interest rate per cent per annum is 5 times the number of years. If the rate of interest increases by 3%, then how much will the simple interest (in ₹) be on ₹5,600 for 6 years?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since Simple Interest (SI) is 1/5 of the principal, total interest earned is 20%.

Given Rate (R) = 5 × Time (T), the total interest percentage = R × T = 5T² = 20%.

⇒ T² = 4 ⇒ T = 2 years ⇒ Initial Rate (R) = 5 × 2 = 10% p.a.

New Rate = 10% + 3% = 13% p.a.

New SI for 6 years = 13% × 6 = 78% of ₹5,600 = ₹4,368.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4368.**
